name: Victims Family
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: Two Santa Rosa teenagers started a trio in 1984, drew a one-year Canadian ban, and landed a Dutch radio hit. At home, Green Day and Mr. Bungle were the openers.

eras.title: A mailed cassette books the first tour
eras.text: Ralph Spight and Larry Boothroyd were teenagers when they started a trio in Santa Rosa. A cassette demo booked a national tour, and Jello Biafra caught them at the Novato Theater.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Music Life Radio · CBS San Francisco: 40th anniversary · Grokipedia
years.h: Santa Rosa teenagers name their band after a Kliban cartoon
years.p: Spight on guitar and vocals and Boothroyd on bass start with drummer Devon VrMeer. CBS San Francisco calls them "scrawny Santa Rosa teenagers."
years.xp:
The name comes from a cartoon by B. Kliban, according to the 2014 Music Life Radio profile of Spight. Wikipedia says the first show was at the Kennilworth Recreation Center in Petaluma.

Grokipedia dates the founding to October 1984; the other sources say only 1984.

years.h: A mailed cassette books a national tour and gets Biafra's attention
years.p: Booked off tapes alone, the trio plays Albuquerque with [[NOFX|dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4]], then opens for the [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]] and the [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]] at the Novato Theater.
years.xp:
Wikipedia has Social Unrest on the Novato bill too, and says that is where [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] noticed the band. Earlier on the run, in Dallas, they challenged Tales of Terror to a drinking contest.

Wikipedia adds that early gigs included opening for Faith No More and Suicidal Tendencies.

years.src: AllMusic: Victims Family · CBS San Francisco: 40th anniversary · Victims Family: Biography · Wikipedia: Victims Family
years.h: Mordam Records puts out Voltage and Violets
years.p: The debut LP took on homophobia when few punk records did, CBS San Francisco notes.
years.xp:
Mordam was Ruth Schwartz's label, and per AllMusic it ended up releasing their first three albums. The band's own site calls the record an "angry brew of off-kilter rhythms and cut-and-paste histrionics."

Around the same year they opened for the Butthole Surfers and Camper Van Beethoven at the Mabuhay Gardens in San Francisco, per Wikipedia, and played The Farm and Club Foot regularly.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Victims Family: Biography
years.h: Nomeansno meets them in an Oakland pizza parlor
years.p: The Canadian trio and the Santa Rosa trio end up sharing bills for years, and in 1990 Nomeansno's drummer produces a Victims Family record.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the pizza parlor show to 1986 and calls it the start of a lasting friendship. [[John Wright|5530ccc3-9bdc-4472-a356-31d621fc6378]] later produced White Bread Blues and The Germ. In 2009 and 2010 the two bands were still sharing stages.

eras.title: Banned from Canada, big in Amsterdam
eras.text: A one-year ban kept them out of Canada while Amsterdam kept inviting them back. Dutch radio put "Caged Bird" at number 16, and at home Mr. Bungle and Green Day opened for them.

years.h: Canada bars them for a year
years.p: Wikipedia says the ban followed a 1987 U.S. tour they barely finished, which included dates with Capitol Punishment in Fresno and Scratch Acid in Dallas.
years.xp: Wikipedia says they missed their Canadian dates because of the ban and gives no reason for it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · AllMusic: Victims Family · CBS San Francisco: Elbo Room
yt: Live: Things I Hate To Admit, Tribal Area
years.h: Second album, cut at Prairie Sun in Cotati
years.p: Things I Hate to Admit is on Mordam again. It is also the year a friendship with [[Primus|84dc4f23-c0b8-4fe1-bbca-a3993ddc8fc2]] starts, and the two bands share a lot of stages after.
years.xp: Wikipedia has the album recorded at Prairie Sun Studio in 1988 and a 7-inch, Son of a Church Card and Quivering Lip, out on Mordam the same year. AllMusic lists the album as 1989; Wikipedia and CBS San Francisco say 1988.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Grokipedia: Victims Family
yt: Live at the Cotati Cabaret, May 24, 1989, Strand on drums
years.h: Eric Strand takes the kit for a five-week European tour
years.p: Amsterdam's Konkurrent Records invites the band over, and Strand replaces Devon VrMeer, who left to raise a family. Snuff of London support.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's tour notes are short and odd: the band helped break down the Berlin Wall and got strip searched in Norway.

Wikipedia has Strand replaced by roadie [[Tim Solyan|add5effa-1139-4e4b-a880-09d9a90bda00]] after the band came home from Europe. Grokipedia says Strand's stint ended mid-tour over creative differences.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Grokipedia: Victims Family
yt: Live at 924 Gilman Street, Berkeley, Oct 13, 1989
years.h: The roadie moves to the drum stool
years.p: Solyan stays through the busiest touring years and is the drummer on the records from White Bread Blues on.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Solyan took over after the European tour and kept drumming through the height of the touring days. Its infobox lists his first stint as 1989 to 1994.

years.big: "One of the outstanding punk albums of the decade."
years.src: CBS San Francisco: 40th anniversary · Wikipedia: Victims Family · AllMusic: Victims Family · Victims Family: Biography
years.p: That is CBS San Francisco's verdict. Wright, drummer of [[Nomeansno|37e9d7b2-7779-41b2-b2eb-3685351caad3]], produces, and the single "Caged Bird" reaches number 16 on Dutch VPRO radio's chart, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the record got wider critical and commercial attention than the two before it; the band's own bio says it lifted them to headlining slots across Europe and North America. AllMusic dates the album 1991; the band's bio and Wikipedia say 1990.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · CBS San Francisco: Elbo Room
years.h: They back Tad and Nirvana across the Midwest
years.p: Wikipedia has them supporting [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] and [[Tad|867d3fb7-9cd1-47a4-a8f0-de29cdca2004]] on the Midwest leg of a 1990 cross-country tour. Back home, [[Mr. Bungle|277e21a9-2d64-452d-96c4-2d23a7af5891]] and [[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]], then little known, opened for them.
years.xp: CBS San Francisco repeats the Nirvana and Primus bills as the band's calling card. The sources give no dates for the tour.

eras.title: Biafra's label, then ten months off
eras.text: Alternative Tentacles released The Germ. Touring wore the band down, they took a break, and the Kennel Club in San Francisco sold out the night they came back.

years.cap: Cover art "Yellow Head" by Harvey Stafford
years.src: Wikipedia: The Germ (album) · AllMusic: Victims Family · Wikipedia: Victims Family
yt: Live at The Axiom, Houston, Feb 19, 1992 (full set)
years.h: Jello Biafra's Alternative Tentacles gets its first Victims Family record
years.p: The Germ runs 17 tracks in 38 minutes, produced again by Wright. Wikipedia says the band left Mordam for the move.
years.xp:
The Germ is credited to Alternative Tentacles and Konkurrent. AllMusic gave it 2.5 stars, called it a break from traditional hardcore, and heard Screaming Trees and Meat Puppets in places. Track titles include I Pissed on a Tree.

Touring took its toll and the band took a break after the record, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Alternative Tentacles: Victims Family
years.h: Ten months off, then a sold-out Kennel Club
years.p: Back in San Francisco in the spring, the band fills the Kennel Club.
years.xp: Wikipedia has them reforming about ten months after the break began, with the "Maybe if I..." 7-inch on Alternative Tentacles to follow. Alternative Tentacles' bio also puts the breakup down to road fatigue.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · Alternative Tentacles: Victims Family
years.h: Headache Remedy lands a year after the comeback
years.p: Fifth album, on Alternative Tentacles, out in February.
years.xp: Scaruffi dates it 1993; Wikipedia and the band's bio say 1994.

years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · AllMusic: Victims Family
years.h: Their "home from home," the Melkweg, is where the first run ends
years.p: Wikipedia has Four Great Thrash Songs recorded live at the Amsterdam club in 1994 and released in 1995. AllMusic says the band disbanded around 1995.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls the Melkweg show the final one for that line-up. Its infobox lists Solyan's first stint as 1989 to 1994.

eras.title: Spight and Boothroyd keep busy elsewhere
eras.text: Other bands filled the gap, Saturn's Flea Collar and Hellworms among them. Then came Apocalicious, with a new drummer.

years.cap: Ralph Spight onstage in San Francisco, December 12, 2004
years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · AllMusic: Victims Family · Victims Family: Biography
years.h: David Gleza of My Name drums on Apocalicious
years.p: After Hellworms fold, Spight and Boothroyd bring Gleza in for a new album on Alternative Tentacles, then tour it through two SXSW trips and two European runs.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the touring wore Gleza out, and Spight and Boothroyd chose not to replace him. The band went on indefinite hiatus.

The years apart include Saturn's Flea Collar and Hellworms, per Wikipedia and the band's bio. The same year brought a split 7-inch with the Fleshies, with the song Dr. Schlesinger.

eras.title: Twenty years in, they keep coming back
eras.text: A twentieth-anniversary weekend in 2004 started a habit. They toured Europe, put out a 2012 single, and finished a split LP for year forty.

years.cap: Larry Boothroyd on bass, San Francisco, December 12, 2004
years.src: Bottom of the Hill: 2004 · Wikipedia: Victims Family
years.h: Twenty years in, they play the Phoenix Theatre and Bottom of the Hill
years.p: Two nights, Petaluma then San Francisco, celebrating every incarnation of the band. Solyan is back on drums for both.
years.xp:
Bottom of the Hill's own calendar confirms the December 12 night. Wikipedia lists the incarnations on the bills: Spight's The Freak Accident, Boothroyd's Meowmeow and the Meowmeows, plus Saturn's Flea Collar and Hellworms reunions.

Those shows led to more of both bands. Wikipedia's infobox lists Solyan as drummer from 2004 to the present.

years.cap: Larry Boothroyd at the Melkweg, Amsterdam, May 19, 2012
years.h: A friend's 50th birthday sends them to the Czech Republic
years.p: They share the bill with Nomeansno and Japan's Le Silo, plus Cuban dancers and typewriter players, and the trip grows into nine shows in nine days.
years.xp: A year earlier, in 2009, they played Alternative Tentacles' 30th anniversary shows in San Francisco with Alice Donut and Jello Biafra and the Guantanamo School of Medicine, and the Phoenix Theater in Petaluma with Nomeansno, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Victims Family at the Melkweg, Amsterdam, May 19, 2012
years.src: Wikipedia: Victims Family · CBS San Francisco: Elbo Room
years.h: "Have a Nice Day" comes out and Finland gets its first show
years.p: The May tour runs 13 shows across Europe, Finland included for the first time.
years.xp: The 7-inch on Alternative Tentacles pairs Have a Nice Day with Let's Cancel the Future. It was the band's last new music until 2024, according to CBS San Francisco.

years.src: CBS San Francisco: 40th anniversary · Wikipedia: Victims Family
years.h: In the Modern Meatspace ends a twelve-year wait
years.p: A split 12-inch with Portland's Nasalrod, out on Nadine Records, run by Nasalrod bassist Mandy Morgan. The two bands met in January 2019.
years.xp:
Wikipedia has a ten-show West Coast run with Nasalrod in 2019, and each band writing five songs for the split by 2022. Nasalrod's drummer is Spit Stix of Fear.

The band marked forty years with a sold-out show at the Big Easy in Petaluma on November 30, per CBS San Francisco. That month they also opened three Pinback shows, including their first Fillmore night since 1994, and in December played three Canadian dates with Dead Bob, John Wright's band.
